quiz_title: 🧊 البرمجة ثلاثية الأبعاد للصغار - PicToBlox 3D - Challenge 2

questions.question: What must you do to make a 3D object fall down, bounce, and collide realistically in your game?
options: Enable physics property for that object
questions.explanation: Correct! Enabling physics makes the computer apply gravity, mass, friction, and collisions to the object.

questions.question: Which force pulls all physical objects downward toward the ground coordinate in a physics simulation?
questions.explanation: Excellent! Gravity is the force that pulls physical objects down toward the floor.

questions.question: Which physical property determines how high a ball will rebound or leap when it impacts the ground?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The bounce value (restitution) controls how much energy is retained during impacts, creating bouncy rebounds.

questions.question: Which physical property creates resistance and slows down an object as it slides across a flat floor?
questions.explanation: Spot on! Friction acts as a braking force, slowing down sliding blocks or rolling balls.

questions.question: What occurs if you set an object's bounce value to '1'?
options: It bounces back up with 100% of its speed, preserving all its height
questions.explanation: Correct! A bounce value of 1 represents a perfectly elastic collision, returning full height.

questions.question: What occurs if you set an object's bounce value to '0'?
options: It hits the ground and stops dead without rebounding at all
questions.explanation: Great! A bounce of 0 means the object retains no kinetic rebound, landing flat.

questions.question: Which block is used to activate forces (push impulses) on a physical object in a specific direction?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'apply force' block delivers a directional push (impulse) along X, Y, or Z axes.

questions.question: In a physics game, what happens when a ball lands on an inclined slope with low friction?
options: It slides down the slope smoothly due to gravity and low friction
questions.explanation: Perfect! Low friction allows gravity to slide the physical ball down the slope with ease.

questions.question: What happens if a physical sprite touches another physical sprite during simulation?
options: They trigger a collision event, stopping or bouncing off each other
questions.explanation: Spot on! Collisions prevent physical bodies from intersecting, causing realistic bounces and shifts.

questions.question: To make a flat ground block that supports other falling boxes without falling itself under gravity, what type of physics object must it be?
questions.explanation: Perfect! A static physical body is solid and triggers collisions but is locked in place, never falling down.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write physics block pseudo-code to enable physics on a sprite named 'Ball1' and set its bounce property to 0.8.
questions.task_hint: enable physics for('Ball1') -> set bounce value of('Ball1') to 0.8
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Enabling physics first allows Ball1 to recognize bounce values, creating realistic rebounds.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write physics block pseudo-code to apply an upward physical force of 500 units along the Y-axis to push a sprite named 'Rocket' upward.
questions.task_hint: apply force X(0) Y(500) Z(0) to('Rocket')
questions.explanation: Perfect! Applying positive Y force propels the physics body vertically into the air!
